  Terse gloss: "ashes; the powdery residue left after burning, often used in rituals of mourning or purification"
  Readable gloss: "The Greek term for ashes—what remains after fire has consumed wood or other combustibles. In the NT it appears in Jesus' reproach against Galilean cities (Matt 11:21, Luke 10:13), saying Tyre and Sidon would have repented 'in sackcloth and ashes,' and in Hebrews 9:13 regarding the ritual use of heifer ashes for purification. Ashes symbolize mourning, repentance, and human frailty ('dust to dust'). Sprinkling ashes on one's head or sitting in ashes expressed grief and contrition, making visible an inner posture of humility before God."

Jesus' counterfactual statement assumes His hearers know this penitential practice—ashes as the physical expression of brokenness and the recognition of mortality.
    Existing Spanish translations: ceniza
